terms.gloss: instead of, in place of, for
evidence: Plaut. Most. 1131b: ego ībō prō tē, sī tibi nōn libet
Ter. And. 200: ego prō tē molam
terms.comment: One person or thing put in the place of another (Lewis & Short: “with the notion of replacement or substitution”).

terms.grammar: conjunctions, joining any two parts of a sentence
evidence: Gell. 7.13.2: nōn cuppēdiās cibōrum, sed argūtiās quaestiōnum
Hor. S. 2.2.120–121: nōn piscibus urbe petītīs, sed pullō atque haedō
terms.comment: Where English says “instead of doing”, Latin sets the two side by side: not this, but that. To prefer one action to another, potius quam (see rather).

terms.grammar: ablative of locus, with a genitive
evidence: Cic. Fam. 7.3.6: crīminis locō putent esse quod vīvam
terms.comment: Something counted as, or standing in for, something else.

phrases.latin: Quīn venīs? — Prōmitte: ego ībō prō tē, sī tibi nōn libet.
phrases.english: Why won’t you come? — Say yes: I’ll go instead of you, if you don’t feel like it.

phrases.latin: conjectābāmus ad cēnulam nōn cuppēdiās cibōrum, sed argūtiās quaestiōnum
phrases.english: to our little dinner we each brought, instead of delicacies, clever questions

sources: Lewis & Short: pro · Lewis & Short: sed · Lewis & Short: locus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 333.
